intent: The oil misdirect: Saudi Arabia is the name, Russia the size, but Venezuela holds the most proven oil on Earth — shown as bars, located as a drawn belt along the Orinoco, and undercut by a split between what it holds and what it pumps.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where is the MOST oil in the world?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where is the most oil in the world?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Venezuela. More than 300 billion barrels of proven oil sit under it, more than any other country on Earth.

lines.direction: pull right out so Venezuela and Saudi Arabia share one frame; Saudi lights dim with its tag on 'Saudi'; the four-row bar chart grows on 'billion'; a shrug sticker on 'Russia'
lines.text: Saudi Arabia is second with about 267 billion. Russia is far down the list.

lines.direction: push deep into eastern Venezuela; from 'Orinoco' the belt line draws itself east along the river; the tag on 'strip'; a tar-drop sticker and a pulse on 'river'
lines.text: Nearly all of it lies in the Orinoco Belt, a strip of heavy, tar-like crude along a single river.

lines.direction: settle back on the country; the HOLDS / PUMPS split slides in on 'pumps'; the pump sticker on 'percent'; the thinking flag-ball and a last pulse on 'underground'
lines.text: Yet it pumps barely 1 percent of the world's oil; the richest reserve on Earth mostly stays underground.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Richer than you thought. Follow us.
